edition.alertText: US reportedly strikes Iranian missile launchers at Bandar Lengeh and Sirik — wider Air Force presence over Persian Gulf (Euronews); UKMTO reports 2 tanker attacks Nov 16: ON PHOENIX (Panama-flagged) struck by projectile in Hormuz — engine-room fire; second tanker disabled near Khasab with engine-room fire; IRGC claims 6 tankers hit mines in 48 hours (Nov 15-16) — none confirmed by CENTCOM or UKMTO; Israel security cabinet meets on Iran for first time in a month — reports say 'could authorize military action'; Iran refuses UN inspections of damaged nuclear sites until war ends; air defenses activated in Isfahan (Mehr); oil crashes ~4% — Brent falls to $91.82 (-4.19%), WTI to $85.04 (-3.98%); third straight weekly decline; gold falls to $3,859/oz — one-year low; silver crashes 3.7% to $46.97; VLCC supertanker rates plunge 64% from October peak (Baltic Exchange); US SPR falls to 276.4M bbl — lowest since 1982; Araghchi at ECO Islamabad, heads to Muscat Tuesday for Hormuz shipping talks with Oman FM Albusaidi; Trump heading to Manila for ASEAN, then Shenzhen for Xi-Putin trilateral (Nov 19) — Iran on agenda; Houthis advance within 60-70 km of Aden — seize Bab el-Mandeb coast; Saudi names new anti-Houthi coalition commander; Houthis launch 2 drones at Mecca and Riyadh; Saudi coalition intercepts; Bahrain sentences defendants to 15 years to life over IRGC links; Jordan blocks Telegram over national security; France expects EU sanctions on Iran in December over IRGC supermarket refrigeration hack; Bessent: Iran economy to shrink 25% Mar 2026-Mar 2027; JMIC: 83 US-escorted transits Nov 12-14 (~28/day), zero unescorted; 3 carriers + ~19 warships in theater; US intelligence estimates Iran has 1,500-2,500 missiles remaining (low confidence, WSJ); 66 km² oil slick spotted near Hormuz on satellite imagery — single source, no exact location confirmed; PBoC bought 26 tonnes of gold in October — 24th straight month of buying; IEA expects Q4 oil surplus as ME exports recover; OPEC+ meets Nov 29 on 2027 output

situation: The military tempo intensified on Monday even as diplomacy positioned for the week's signature event — the Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral summit in Shenzhen on November 19. Reports from Euronews cited US strikes on Iranian missile launchers at Bandar Lengeh and Sirik on Sunday night, with flight-tracking data showing a much larger US Air Force presence over the Persian Gulf than in previous weeks; CENTCOM has not confirmed the strikes. Israel's security cabinet convened on Iran for the first time in more than a month, with reports suggesting it 'could authorize military action,' while the Mossad chief continued talks in Washington pressing for renewed strikes on Iran's nuclear program. Iran responded with continued drone and mine activity: Bahrain confirmed intercepting IRGC drones for the second time in three days, and Iran's military warned that its new offensive doctrine will end calculated retaliation limits, with threats extending to US bases in Europe via modified Khorramshahr-4 missiles (3,000-4,000 km range). Iran stated it will not allow UN inspections of damaged nuclear sites until the war ends, and air defenses were activated in Isfahan on Monday. Araghchi arrived in Islamabad for an ECO foreign ministers' meeting and is scheduled to visit Muscat on Tuesday for talks with Oman's FM Albusaidi on restoring shipping through Hormuz — building on the Iran-Oman understanding to jointly oversee the strait. Trump departed for Manila and the ASEAN summit ahead of the Shenzhen meeting, where Iran will be a central agenda item alongside nuclear arms control; no separate Trump-Putin bilateral is planned. Treasury Secretary Bessent projected Iran's economy will contract 25% from March 2026 to March 2027 under the blockade.

Oil prices crashed on Monday as the supply surplus narrative overwhelmed persistent attack risk. Brent fell 4.19% to $91.82/bbl — its lowest since the November 9 'war effectively over' plunge — while WTI dropped 3.98% to $85.04/bbl, with CNBC reporting US crude 'declines to $85 a barrel on recovering Middle East exports.' The sell-off extended oil's November decline to approximately 20% from the October peak, with Goldman Sachs declaring the oil market's $27 war premium effectively gone. The IEA projected the global oil market will return to surplus in Q4 2026 as Middle East exports recover faster than demand, and OPEC+ is set to meet November 29 to decide 2027 output policy. The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell to 276.4 million barrels — the lowest since 1982 — after the DOE released reserves under a 172-million-barrel agreement. VLCC supertanker rates plunged 64% from their October 8 peak, with the Gulf of Oman–China rate falling from 841 Worldscale to 308 WS on November 13 (Baltic Exchange), driven by what Arrow Shipbroking called an 'exaggerated unwinding of the geopolitical risk premium.' Gold fell to $3,859/oz — a one-year low — down 0.64% on the day, while silver crashed 3.7% to $46.97/oz, its lowest in over a year. The gold-silver ratio widened past 82, and precious metals posted their worst weekly performance in four months as expectations of further US rate hikes intensified. China's PBoC bought 26 tonnes of gold in October, its largest monthly purchase since August 2023 and 24th straight month of buying, with holdings at 2,435 tonnes.

Shipping attacks continued at a near-daily pace. UKMTO reported two tanker attacks on November 16: the ON PHOENIX (Panama-flagged, IMO 9893228) was struck by an unidentified projectile while transiting outbound through Hormuz at approximately 0558 UTC, causing an engine-room fire with all crew accounted for and no casualties; a second tanker was attacked about 7 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman at approximately 1900 UTC, also resulting in an engine-room fire and vessel disabled, with the crew reported safe. JMIC counted five attacks off Oman's Musandam Peninsula since November 1, while an independent count (IMO/UKMTO data only) logged 57 attacks on 56 vessels in 60 days, including 42 tankers. The IRGC claimed six tankers hit mines in the 48 hours spanning November 15-16, though none have been independently confirmed — UKMTO's 'projectile' classification does not match Iran's mine claims. JMIC data from November 12-14 showed 83 US-escorted transits (approximately 28 per day), about 20% of the pre-war baseline of roughly 138 daily crossings, with zero unescorted tankers. Satellite imagery reportedly revealed a 66 km² oil slick near Hormuz from a single source, though no exact location has been confirmed. In Yemen, the Houthi advance toward Aden accelerated — forces now within 60-70 km of the city after seizing positions along the Bab el-Mandeb coast, creating dual-chokepoint control over both Hormuz (via Iran) and the Red Sea approaches. Saudi Arabia named a new commander for the anti-Houthi coalition as Houthi drones targeted Mecca and Riyadh, intercepted by Saudi defenses. US intelligence estimates Iran retains 1,500 to 2,500 missiles (low confidence, per the Wall Street Journal), against a pre-war CENTCOM estimate of approximately 3,000.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne — more than doubled since pre-war — feeding into phosphate production costs; Egypt, Brazil, India cutting output. Mosaic phosphate plants remain curtailed including South Fort Meade (Florida) — 199 workers laid off. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%; DAP at $803/mt in October, ~30% above January (IFDC). Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst). China phosphate exports near zero in 2026, down from ~5.3M mt in 2025 (IFDC).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for fourth consecutive month — September, October, and early November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). UN official Jorge Moreira da Silva at COP31 (Nov 14) warns 45 million people could face severe food insecurity — urges US and Iran to immediately allow ~5 fertilizer vessels/day through Hormuz within 7-10 days. Fertilizer prices up ~30% since blockades began (UN). Sudan food prices doubled in 6 months; Nepal farmers cannot afford fertiliser. Countries facing significant impact: Mozambique, Kenya, Sudan, Somalia, Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka. Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). DAP at $803/mt in October, urea near January levels after April spike (IFDC Bulletin #37). Egypt gas supply cuts to fertilizer producers rose from 20% to 33% on Nov 8 — AGF Nitrogen running at 80-85% capacity (IFDC). Russia export quotas Dec 2026–May 2027 at ~18.8M mt, down from ~20M mt. IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Middle East fertiliser exports declined by 70% as Iran war disrupts supplies (The National).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Qatar LNG loadings pick up to roughly half of pre-war levels (Bloomberg, Nov 10). Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas eased to ~€89.59/MWh (~$100.85), down from 4-year high above €101/MWh prior week; EU gas storage at 74.33% full vs 86% five-year average — lowest in over a decade entering winter (IEA). LNG crossings at Hormuz reached 32 in October — highest since war began (S&P Global). IRGC claims gas carrier exploded after mine strike in eastern Hormuz (Nov 13). Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war. Europe and Asia face tight supply heading into winter. JERA CEO says Qatar LNG supply unlikely to recover soon. EIA projects US heating oil households to pay $2,977 this winter — up 70.2% from last year. IMF projects 2026 GDP contractions: Kuwait and Iraq ~16%, Qatar ~15%.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B on energy surge. Aramco Q3 profit surges 34.6% to $36.3B. Allianz Trade estimates >$200B in physical damage across GCC — 80+ energy facilities struck, a third severely damaged; cumulative economic losses projected at $790B through 2030.
